name: Notion (public connections / OAuth)
summary: Notion now calls integrations 'connections' and manages them in the Developer portal (app.notion.com/developers/connections). A public (OAuth) connection needs no approval to work for real users: create it, pick an installation scope, add redirect URIs, and you get a client ID/secret in minutes. Only an optional Marketplace listing is reviewed (Notion says 5-10 business days). The real constraint for AI agents is the page picker: your agent only ever sees the pages each user explicitly shares.

verdict.headline: 1-3 hours to a working OAuth connection with no approval; +1-2 weeks only if you want a Marketplace listing
verdict.rationale: Public connections work over OAuth for any user as soon as they are created; Notion states Marketplace listing is optional and separate. There is no scope-verification process comparable to Google's. The friction is product-level, not approval-level: each user must individually authorize and choose pages in the page picker, the installation scope ('Any workspace' vs 'Selected workspaces only') is permanent, Enterprise owners can block or allow-list connections, and capability changes force users to re-authenticate.

evidence.quote: Listing on the Marketplace is optional and helps your connection reach a wider audience
evidence.note: Marketplace FAQ explicitly says public connections work via OAuth without being listed.

effort.approvalNote: No approval is needed to create or use a public connection with real users. Review happens only if you submit a Marketplace listing (Listings > Connections); the Notion team reviews every submission, including a security review, and says to expect an email reply within 5-10 business days. Rejections can be fixed and resubmitted, which restarts the wait.

evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email
evidence.note: 5-10 business days converted to roughly 1-2 calendar weeks; this is time to first response, not guaranteed approval.

paths.name: Internal connection (your own workspace only)
paths.when: You only need the agent to work in a workspace you own/administer (prototype, internal tool). Not usable for other people's workspaces.
paths.whatChanges: No OAuth: a static API token from the Configuration tab. You must be a Workspace Owner to create it. Pages are granted via the Content access tab or each page's ••• > Connections > Add connection. Subject to the Free-plan 1,000-block limit on multi-member Free workspaces. (A personal access token is a similar single-user alternative for scripts.)

evidence.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

paths.name: Public connection, 'Selected workspaces only' (OAuth, private beta/design partners)
paths.when: You want real OAuth with per-user tokens but only for specific known workspaces (e.g. a pilot customer). Cannot ever be listed on the Marketplace.
paths.whatChanges: Same OAuth implementation as the unlisted public path, but you choose the allowed workspaces at creation. Scope is permanent: to go Marketplace later you must create a new connection (new client ID/secret, users re-authorize). These connections are subject to the Free workspace block limit.

evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time

paths.name: Public connection, 'Any workspace', not listed (default for an AI agent product)
paths.when: Your product lets any Notion user connect their workspace via an 'Add to Notion'/Connect button. This is the most common path.
paths.whatChanges: Choose 'Any workspace' at creation (keeps the Marketplace option open), add HTTPS redirect URIs, pick minimal capabilities, implement code exchange + refresh-token rotation. No review needed before real users can install.

evidence.quote: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token

paths.name: Public connection listed on the Notion Marketplace
paths.when: You want discoverability in Notion's connections gallery (notion.com/integrations / Settings > Connections).
paths.whatChanges: Requires an 'Any workspace' connection plus a listing (name, description, category, tags, images, logo) submitted from Listings > Connections. Notion reviews every listing and public connections undergo a security review; rejections cite brand/trademark, quality, or baseline-criteria issues.

appModel.providerTerm: Public connection (formerly 'public integration') in the Notion Developer portal
appModel.explanation: One public connection = your product. Each end user who completes OAuth creates their own authorization (a bot_id) scoped to one workspace and to only the pages they selected in the page picker. If five members of one workspace want to use your agent, each must authorize individually; one user's grant does not cover teammates. The access token acts on behalf of the authorizing user, but can only touch pages shared with the connection (plus their children).
appModel.tokenNotes: Token exchange at POST https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token (HTTP Basic auth with client_id:client_secret) returns access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id, owner. Refresh tokens now exist: grant_type=refresh_token returns a NEW access token AND a NEW refresh token, so always persist the latest pair. Since 2026-06-08, new public connections mint a fresh token pair on every authorization (including re-auth) instead of returning the existing one. The REST docs do not state an access-token lifetime and the token response documents no expires_in; build refresh-on-401 rather than assuming tokens never expire. Changing capabilities forces users to re-authenticate. (Hosted Notion MCP is separate: its tokens last ~8 hours and use dynamic client registration.)

evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token

steps.title: Pick connection type and installation scope
steps.actorNote: An agent can lay out the trade-offs; you make the irreversible scope choice.
instructions: Internal connection: only your own workspace, static token, no OAuth.
Public connection with 'Any workspace': any Notion user can install via OAuth; Marketplace-eligible. Default choice for an AI agent product.
Public connection with 'Selected workspaces only': OAuth restricted to chosen workspaces; never Marketplace-eligible and subject to Free-plan block limits.
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation - switching later means a new connection and every user re-authorizing.

evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Developer portal
steps.actorNote: Requires your Notion login; an agent can draft the name and redirect URIs.
instructions: Open the Developer portal at app.notion.com/developers/connections.
In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.
Click Create new connection.
Enter the connection name and choose your development workspace.
Add your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section (exact match, HTTPS in production).
Choose installation scope: Any workspace or Selected workspaces only (then select workspaces).

Select capabilities: tick only Read content / Update content / Insert content and comment capabilities you need; choose the user-information level (prefer 'User information without email addresses' unless you need email).
Save/create the connection.

values.note: Must exactly match the redirect_uri you send in the authorize and token requests.
Keeps the Marketplace option open; cannot be changed later.

targets.hint: Capability checkbox - request only what you need

evidence.quote: including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section

steps.title: Copy OAuth client ID, client secret and authorization URL
steps.actorNote: Secrets are only visible to you in the logged-in portal; paste them into your secret manager, never into code or chat.
instructions: Open your connection and go to the Configuration tab.
Copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret into environment variables (e.g. OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET).
Copy the Authorization URL if shown. If the field is empty, build it yourself: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&owner=user&redirect_uri=...&state=...

targets.hint: Holds client ID, secret, capabilities and Basic information
Public identifier used in the authorize URL
May stay empty until the connection is submitted for review - build the URL manually

evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

steps.title: Implement authorize, code exchange and refresh-token rotation
steps.actorNote: Pure code work an AI agent can do end to end once secrets are in env vars.
instructions: Send users to the authorize URL with owner=user, response_type=code and a random state; verify state on return.
Handle error=access_denied on the redirect (user pressed Cancel).
POST the code to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code (include redirect_uri if it was in the authorize URL or you registered several).
Persist access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id, workspace_name and owner per authorization; store every new pair, including on re-authorization.
Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token; replace BOTH tokens with the response (refresh tokens rotate). On invalid_grant, send the user back through OAuth.
Send Notion-Version header on API calls and handle 429 with Retry-After.

evidence.quote: Refreshes an access token, generating a new access token and new refresh token

steps.title: Design the agent around the page picker
steps.actorNote: Agent can build the UX and empty-state handling; you decide whether to ship a template.
instructions: Tell users before redirecting: 'Select pages' then 'Allow access' - the agent can only see pages they pick (and their children).
Handle the zero-pages case: after connecting, call Search; if empty, prompt the user to re-run OAuth or add the connection to pages via ••• > Connections.
Optionally set 'Notion URL for optional template' (Configuration tab > Basic information) so users can duplicate a starter page that is shared with your connection automatically.
Remember the picker only shows pages the user has full access to, and each workspace member must authorize separately.

steps.title: Create an internal connection (single-workspace path)
instructions: In the Developer portal, under Build, select Internal connections.
Click Create a new connection, enter a name, choose the workspace.
Open the Configuration tab and copy the API token; set capabilities.
Open the Content access tab, click Edit access, and select pages/databases (a new connection has no access by default).

evidence.quote: A newly created connection has no page access by default.

steps.title: Create and submit a Marketplace listing
steps.actorNote: Agent can draft description, tags and image specs; you upload assets, confirm brand/trademark rights and submit.
instructions: Open the Marketplace listing dashboard (notion.so/profile/connections).
In the Listings section of the sidebar, select Connections.
Under Drafts, click Start a new connection listing.
Fill in listing name and description, category and tags, listing images and logo, and associate your 'Any workspace' public connection.
Save as draft, review everything, then submit for review; the listing moves to Submitted.
Watch email for feedback (5-10 business days); fix and resubmit if rejected.

blockers.title: Agent 'can't find' a page the user expects
blockers.symptom: API returns object_not_found / empty Search results even though the page exists in the user's workspace.
blockers.fix: The page was not selected in the page picker (or is not a child of a selected page). Ask the user to re-run the OAuth flow and select it, or add your connection via the page's ••• > Connections menu. Users can only share pages they have full access to.

evidence.quote: The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has

blockers.title: Wrong installation scope chosen
blockers.symptom: You picked 'Selected workspaces only' and now cannot list on the Marketplace or install for new customers.
blockers.fix: Scope can't be edited. Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace', migrate redirect URIs/secrets, and have users re-authorize.

evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time

blockers.title: Refresh fails with invalid_grant after a refresh
blockers.symptom: Second refresh using the original refresh_token fails.
blockers.fix: Refresh tokens rotate: persist the new refresh_token from every refresh and every re-authorization atomically; serialize refreshes per authorization.

evidence.quote: Store the token pair from every successful response

blockers.title: Enterprise workspace blocks your connection
blockers.symptom: Users on Enterprise plans cannot find or install your connection.
blockers.fix: Workspace owners can restrict installs to an approved list. Ask the customer's workspace owner to approve your connection in Settings > Connections > Manage; request minimal capabilities to ease approval.

evidence.quote: workspace owners can restrict which connections members are allowed to install.

blockers.title: Users forced to re-authorize after you add a capability
blockers.symptom: Existing users' calls fail or they are prompted to reconnect after you change capabilities.
blockers.fix: Decide capabilities up front; if you must change them, ship a reconnect prompt and expect drop-off.

evidence.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed

blockers.title: Block-creation writes fail with 403 on Free workspaces
blockers.symptom: Create page / append blocks fail on a multi-member Free workspace after the 1,000-block limit grace period.
blockers.fix: Applies to internal and 'Selected workspaces only' connections, not 'Any workspace' OAuth connections. Use an 'Any workspace' public connection, or ask the workspace to upgrade.

evidence.quote: The limit applies to internal connections and OAuth connections restricted to selected workspaces

blockers.title: Authorization URL field is empty in the portal
blockers.symptom: Configuration tab shows no Authorization URL for a new public connection.
blockers.fix: Docs say it populates after the connection is submitted for review; you can construct the authorize URL yourself from client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user.

evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

blockers.title: Marketplace listing rejected
blockers.symptom: Email from Notion declining the listing.
blockers.fix: Common causes per Notion: brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or baseline criteria not met. Address feedback and resubmit from Listings > Connections.

evidence.quote: The Notion team reviews every listing submission.

uncertainties: Access-token lifetime for REST public connections is not documented and the token response documents no expires_in; whether access tokens currently expire (and when) could not be verified.

verificationLog.check: Where integrations are created and what they are called
verificationLog.detail: Commonly repeated advice says 'create an integration at notion.so/profile/integrations (or my-integrations)'. Current docs call them 'connections' and send developers to the Developer portal (app.notion.com/developers/connections, launched 2026-05-12) under Build > Public connections / Internal connections. notion.so/profile/connections is now the Marketplace listing dashboard.

verificationLog.check: Do Notion OAuth tokens have refresh tokens / expire?
verificationLog.detail: Older advice: Notion access tokens never expire and there are no refresh tokens. Current docs return a refresh_token on exchange and document grant_type=refresh_token, which rotates both tokens. Since 2026-06-08 new public connections mint a fresh pair per authorization. Access-token lifetime itself remains undocumented.

verificationLog.check: Public vs internal: 'Distribution' tab toggle to make an integration public
verificationLog.detail: Older flow converted an internal integration to public via a Distribution tab with company name, website, privacy policy, terms and support email. Current docs: you create a public connection directly and choose an installation scope (Any workspace / Selected workspaces only) that cannot be changed later; listing details live in a separate Listings section.

Marketplace guide FAQ: reply within 5-10 business days via email; listing is optional; only 'Any workspace' connections are eligible. Overview: public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed.

verificationLog.check: Page picker model and per-user authorization
verificationLog.detail: Users choose pages in the picker; picker shows only pages with full access; each workspace member must authorize individually; access extends to children of shared pages.
Help Center: on Enterprise plans workspace owners can restrict which connections members install and maintain an approved list. Internal connections require Workspace Owner to create.

verificationLog.check: Free workspace block limit applies to API
verificationLog.detail: From 2026-09-01 the REST API enforces the 1,000-block limit on multi-member Free workspaces for internal and 'Selected workspaces only' connections, not 'Any workspace' OAuth connections.

verificationLog.check: Developer portal and dashboard URLs reachable
verificationLog.detail: app.notion.com/developers/connections, notion.so/profile/connections and notion.so/profile/integrations all returned HTTP 200 (unauthenticated; content behind login not inspected).
